domain: The clash between decision-theoretic models of triage and what emergency-room nurses actually do when allocating scarce beds
topic: The clash between decision-theoretic models of triage and what emergency-room nurses actually do when allocating scarce beds

source.title: The thinking style that makes people vulnerable to extremism

movement.gist: Lay out the elegance of formal triage scoring systems (e.g., severity indices, queuing-theory bed allocation) — how they promise to remove bias and inconsistency from life-and-death decisions by converting judgment into calculation.

Introduce the practitioner collision: nurses routinely override the scores based on things the model can't encode — a patient's breathing pattern, a family's demeanor, a gut sense that someone is 'about to turn' — and these overrides often prove right in retrospect.

Refuse both readings: this isn't proof the model is worthless (overrides are sometimes wrong, and unaided judgment has its own catastrophic failure modes) nor proof the nurses just need better-calibrated intuition folded into new variables — the two are answering different questions about what triage even is.
Locate the value not in resolving which side is right but in the friction itself — the override moments are where the actual object of triage becomes visible, which the smooth-running system hides.

primary.axis: formal optimization models of triage vs. the tacit, improvisational judgment of practicing nurses
poles: triage as a solvable allocation problem
triage as an irreducibly situated craft

secondary.axis: whether the failure of the model is a failure of implementation or a failure of the model's premises
poles: the model just needs richer variables
the model is asking the wrong kind of question

tension_system.interaction: the secondary tension prevents the primary one from collapsing into 'practice wins,' because even nurses' objections can't say which kind of failure they're pointing at

family_realization.note: P1 elegance ('severity index converts shivering chaos'), P2-3 collision ('not a verdict...but the override is a fact'), P4 friction locates value ('friction is where the thing being sorted briefly shows its face'). Refuses both wins.

ending_behavior.note: P4 closes by interrogating 'Accuracy,' 'override,' 'failure'—the passage's own tools. Aperture widens: 'no longer trust my instruments.' Refusal suspended, not resolved.

voice_consistency.note: 'I confess I came...prepared to distrust it, and I was disarmed'—suspicious of novelty, honest about tradition's failures. Maintains throughout; no generic register drift.

distractor_efficiency.note: Q1(C): premature_closure trap—reader tempted to stop at P2 'easy' moment. Q2(A): stance_misread—P3 explicitly rejects this move. Q3(A): half_truth—shared word hides, not resolves. Q4(A): scope_inflation. Q5(B): adjacent_answer. Q6(B): straw_version. All traps passage-anchored, not lexically extreme.

explanation_quality.note: Every wrong option tied to specific locations: Q1(B) cites P3's 'two questions' refutation; Q2(B) quotes 'not always right' and 'catastrophic failure modes'; Q3(B) references P4's aperture-widening absence of synthesis. Mechanisms named precisely.

answers.reasoning: Passage centers on override revealing two distinct questions, destabilizing terms of judgment.
Final paragraph explicitly states he no longer trusts his instruments of judgment.
Text explicitly contrasts 'who is sickest' versus 'what counts as sick enough to reorder.'
Author explicitly states this as his own claim, unlike the steelmanned nostalgia or model claims.
Directly stated: suspicion of calculation partly suspicion of his own displacement.
Passage explicitly rejects folding nurse cues into model as new inputs, calling it a category error.
